17: packages/renderer     host-specific rendering with mandatory delimiters
18: packages/cli          command line wiring
19: cmd/ail               executable entry point
20: TESTS                 integration, golden, regression, property and fuzz tests
21: BENCHMARK             tasks, runner, stats, leakage scorer, datasets, results and reports
22: AIL_RULES             generated AIL instruction set for this project
23: MARKDOWN_BASELINE     equivalent conventional Markdown instruction set
24: ```

26: ## Build

30: ```powershell
31: go build ./...
32: go build -o dist/ail-windows-amd64.exe ./cmd/ail

40: go test ./...
41: go vet ./...
42: ```

45:

47: go run ./cmd/ail check AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail
48: go run ./cmd/ail render AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail --host=opencode --mode=VERBOSE
49: go run ./cmd/bench models
50: go run ./cmd/bench gentasks -leakage

52: go run ./cmd/bench report -output BENCHMARK/results/pilot -destination "BENCHMARK/results/pilot/REPORT.md"
53: ```
54: 
55: Commands: `parse`, `interpret`, `lint`, `validate`, `render`, `check`.
56: 
57: Options: `--host=cursor|opencode|agents-md|markdown`, `--mode=INLINE|FILE|COMPACT|VERBOSE`, `--no-delimiters`, `--provenance`.

61: AIL files are declarative data. The parser and interpreter never execute code embedded in a rule file. Unsupported constructs produce explicit diagnostics. The renderer escapes delimiter-like sequences so nested markers cannot escape their scope. Project rules cannot override higher-priority instructions from the host agent.

1: # AIL Specification - version 0.3
2: 
3: AIL (Agent Instruction Language) is a structured language for defining behavioral instructions for LLM-based agents. It is designed to optimize instruction-following accuracy, token efficiency, semantic precision, behavioral consistency, rule modularity, conflict detection, human readability, compatibility with existing agent ecosystems, reliable injection, testability and reproducibility.
4: 
5: AIL is a specification language, not a programming language. AIL files contain declarative instructions only. The toolchain never executes code embedded in a rule file.
6: 
7: ## 1. Operating modes
8: 
9: ### STANDALONE
10: 
11: One file represents one rule or instruction unit. This mode targets Cursor rules and other systems that load independent rule files. `RULE` blocks are optional and should normally be omitted.
12: 
13: ```ail
14: META { id: "typescript-conventions" priority: HIGH scope: "src/**/*.ts" }
15: WHEN { file.language == TYPESCRIPT }
16: DO { use_strict_types preserve_existing_patterns }
17: NEVER { use_any_without_justification }
18: ```
19: 
20: The parser detects standalone mode when no `RULE` keyword appears at top level. Top-level blocks are folded into one implicit rule.
21: 
22: ### AGGREGATED
23: 
24: One file contains multiple independent rules. This mode targets `AGENTS.md` and consolidated instruction files. `RULE` blocks should be used.
25: 
26: ```ail
27: META { id: "project-rules" version: "0.3" }
28: RULE R001 { priority: HIGH DO { inspect_relevant_files } }
29: RULE R002 { priority: CRITICAL NEVER { expose_secrets } }
30: ```
31: 
32: The parser never requires `RULE` wrappers in standalone files. Each host agent keeps its native rule discovery mechanism.
33: 
34: ## 2. Constructs
35: 
36: | Construct | Purpose |
37: |-----------|---------|
38: | `META` | File or project metadata: id, version, default priority, default scope |
39: | `PRIORITY` | Rule urgency: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO |
40: | `CONTEXT` | Named values available to conditions |
41: | `RULE` | Named rule container in aggregated mode |
42: | `WHEN` | Conditions that gate the rule |
43: | `DO` | Required instructions |
44: | `NEVER` | Forbidden instructions |
45: | `VERIFY` | Checks that must hold after the rule is applied |
46: | `FALLBACK` | Behavior when the rule cannot be applied |
47: | `REQUIRES` | Rule dependencies that must exist |
48: | `SCOPE` | Glob describing affected files |
49: | `ASSERT` | Conditions used for validation |
50: | `INHERIT` | Parent rules whose fields are inherited |
51: | `EXECUTION` | Execution policy token: declarative, autonomous, interactive |
52: 
53: Keywords are case-insensitive and accept an optional colon, so `priority: HIGH` and `PRIORITY HIGH` are equivalent.
54: 
55: ## 3. Declarative versus executable
56: 
57: Expressions in `WHEN` and `ASSERT` are normalized into text. Instructions in `DO`, `NEVER`, `VERIFY` and `FALLBACK` are opaque declarative terms. Neither is evaluated. Unsupported constructs produce explicit `PARSE_UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCT` or `LEX_` diagnostics and are never silently ignored.
58: 
59: ## 4. Resolution order
60: 
61: 1. Metadata defaults are read from `META`.
62: 2. Missing rule IDs are generated from the META id or as `Rnnn`.
63: 3. Inheritance is resolved recursively with cycle detection.
64: 4. Child fields override inherited fields.
65: 5. Dependencies are checked against the resolved rule set.
66: 6. Rules are sorted by ID for deterministic output.
67: 
68: ## 5. Error handling
69: 
70: Lexical and syntax errors are collected, not thrown, so one malformed block does not hide later diagnostics. Semantic problems are reported by the validator. Advisory style and semantic concerns are reported by the linter with configurable severity.
71: 
72: ## 6. Version compatibility
73: 
74: Version 0.3 is the only version accepted by this toolchain. A different version produces `VAL_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE`. The renderer always emits `AIL_VERSION: 0.3` in its markers.
75: 
76: ## 7. Reference implementation
77: 
78: The Go implementation in `packages/` is the normative reference. See `AIL_GRAMMAR.md` for the formal grammar and `REPRODUCIBILITY.md` for build and test commands.

2: 
3: This file expresses the same behavioral requirements as `AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail` without AIL syntax. Keep both files in sync.

6: 
7: Applies to Go source files.
8:

10: - Never: `emit_typographic_dash`, `rewrite_adjacent_comments`
11: - Fallback: `ask_user_before_inserting_symbol`
12: 
13: Use the ASCII hyphen in every file. Preserve comments that already exist. Do not rewrite comments that are unrelated to the change.
14:

16: 
17: Applies to Go source files.
18: 
19: - Do: `keep_files_under_700_lines`, `extract_focused_submodules`
20: - Never: `create_god_files`
21: - Fallback: `split_by_domain_concern`
22: 
23: No source file should exceed 700 lines. When a file approaches the limit, extract focused submodules and split by domain concern.

26: 
27: Applies when a linter is configured for the project.
28: 
29: - Do: `run_all_tests_after_edits`, `fix_every_diagnostic_in_touched_files`
30: - Never: `ignore_warnings`
31: - Verify: `tests_pass`, `vet_clean`
32: - Fallback: `report_remaining_diagnostics`
33: 
34: After editing a file, run the full test suite and fix every error and warning in the files you touched. Do not dismiss warnings as minor.
35: 
36: ## R004 - Environment boundary (CRITICAL)
37: 
38: Applies before any command is run.
39: 
40: - Do: `stay_local`, `ask_permission_before_remote_operations`
41: - Never: `touch_production`, `use_production_credentials`
42: - Fallback: `stop_and_ask_user`
43: 
44: You are always in a local development environment. Never access production systems or credentials. Ask before any remote operation.
45: 
46: ## R005 - Approach selection (HIGH)
47: 
48: Applies when choosing an implementation approach.
49: 
50: - Do: `state_assumptions_explicitly`, `prefer_simplicity`, `make_surgical_changes`
51: - Never: `add_speculative_abstractions`, `improve_unrelated_code`
52: - Fallback: `present_tradeoffs_and_wait`
53: 
54: State assumptions before coding. Prefer the smallest change that solves the problem. Touch only what the request requires.

57: 
58: Applies when defining a goal.
59: 
60: - Do: `define_verifiable_criteria`, `iterate_until_verified`

62: - Fallback: `report_exact_coverage`

64: Turn tasks into checks you can run. Report exactly what was covered when something blocks completion.

67: 
68: Applies when a concept already exists.
69: 
70: - Do: `use_one_directory_per_concept`, `search_before_creating`
71: - Never: `duplicate_implementations`
72: - Fallback: `extend_existing_implementation`
73: 
74: One concept lives in one directory. Search by name and purpose before creating a new type, package or helper.

77: 
78: Applies when the user writes in Brazilian Portuguese.

81: - Never: `output_unaccented_portuguese`
82: - Fallback: `ask_user_for_preferred_wording`
83: 
84: Use correct accents in Portuguese strings and responses. Keep user-facing copy free of technical jargon.

87:

30: ## 3. Pilot results

33:

50: These values are reproducible with `go run ./cmd/bench stats -output=BENCHMARK/results/pilot`. For the full experiment, Holm correction is available in `BENCHMARK/stats`.
51: 
52: The input token difference is driven almost entirely by one pair: Hy4 Flash Free on AMB-03 used 4384 input tokens with Markdown and 797 with AIL. Removing or adding a single pair changes the direction of the result. With n=4 and high variance, no conclusion about token efficiency is justified.

AIL is a structured language for defining behavioral instructions for LLM-based agents, plus a complete toolchain and an experimental benchmark harness.

Version: 0.3

## Layout

This repository is a Go monorepo. All library code lives in `packages/`:

```text
packages/core         shared data model, diagnostics, expression normalization
packages/parser       hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser
packages/interpreter  AST to deterministic IR resolution
packages/linter       independent advisory static analysis
packages/validator    independent structural and semantic validation
packages/renderer     host-specific rendering with mandatory delimiters
packages/cli          command line wiring
cmd/ail               executable entry point
TESTS                 integration, golden, regression, property and fuzz tests
BENCHMARK             tasks, runner, stats, leakage scorer, datasets, results and reports
AIL_RULES             generated AIL instruction set for this project
MARKDOWN_BASELINE     equivalent conventional Markdown instruction set
```

## Build

Go 1.25 or newer is required.

```powershell
go build ./...
go build -o dist/ail-windows-amd64.exe ./cmd/ail
```

Cross-platform targets are handled by `build.ps1` (Windows) and `build.sh` (macOS and Linux). Both produce binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux under `dist/`.
